events: day1 reliably identified bird A has only nonconfirming evidence at old nest
day3 same-sex A uniquely resolves through IN at new nest
cases.expected: Omit only old nest's level-zero A candidate; retain new confirmed A and both nests. No raw observation is changed.

events: old nest has evidence on the same date as or after the new proof
cases.expected: Keep the earlier-nest candidate; dates cannot establish same-day observation order.

events: A already independently resolved at old nest, including three nonconfirming observations
later A confirms at new nest
cases.expected: Keep both established historical associations; no automatic global winner or proof transfer.

events: later claim is opposite sex, a different identity, ambiguous, tied, X-X, a shared recruit mark, or beyond reference date
cases.expected: No cross-nest suppression. Only an unambiguous uniquely selected level-2 or level-3 result on a reliable same-sex identity can supply proof.

events: old nest has two weak candidates A and B
later A confirms at new nest
cases.expected: Omit A at old nest, retain B as pending rather than resolved, and recount the former weak-candidate tie.
Preserve A's independently earned proof and date.
A qualifies through three; no universal post-MM reset.
X-X, not MM-only A, is associated.

events: zero to two later eligible B sightings
cases.expected: B cannot inherit X-X proof; retain the X-X placeholder.
B independently qualifies on day6; one unique candidate retires earlier X-X without transferring proof.
B independently qualifies on day4, never backdated to day2.

events: MM-only A with partial nonconfirming proof
A accumulates a third nonconfirming sighting
cases.expected: Retiring the placeholder does not revive excluded MM-only A.
Preserve independently established evidence and apply ordinary ranking/ambiguity; do not automatically certify B.

cases.label: sameDayXXIN + firstMM
events: day1 exactly one eligible capture_status F MM captured identity of same sex and nest
cases.expected: Assume targeted same individual; transfer same-day confirmation and resolve marked identity on day1. Preserve observation date; linked proof uses capture datetime conservatively, with no exact observed time/order inferred.

events: day2 unique eligible capture_status F MM capture of same sex and nest
no own confirming or three distinct eligible postcapture observations
cases.expected: New marked identity stays pending; no transfer of day1 proof and no retirement based on capture alone.

events: day2 eligible X-X IN and unique eligible capture_status F MM capture of same sex and nest
cases.expected: Own day2 same-day linkage confirms marked identity and permits retirement of older placeholder without transferring day1 proof; proof is dated at day2 capture datetime.

events: two competing eligible capture_status F captured identities of same sex and nest
cases.expected: No unique same-day link; retain uncertainty under existing hierarchy/ambiguity rules.

events: two eligible F capture identity keys at same sex/nest/date in first_marking_counts before later-proof or ambiguity filters
one candidate lacks later proof or is excluded by a later ambiguity filter
cases.expected: The first-marking pool still contains two distinct capture identity keys; later filtering cannot manufacture a unique replacement or authorize same-day proof transfer. Count keys, not duplicate rows; confirming resighting r must also be unambiguous.

events: same-day X-X/capture pair with ambiguous or ineligible evidence, other sex/nest, recapture only, or capture/proof beyond reference date
cases.expected: No same-day proof transfer; all eligibility and reference-date guards still apply.

events: day1 same-day X-X IN and unique eligible first MM capture link
day2 same-sex X-X IN at that nest
cases.expected: Day2 X-X remains separate evidence; original displacement history and independent strong conflicts are preserved.

events: duplicates, future proof, ambiguous matches, opposite-sex X-X, later recapture, or multiple qualifying candidates
cases.expected: No duplicate inflation, future leakage, opposite-sex displacement, or unsupported X-X identity transfer.
